summary: Round 3 (fit bug fixed: target centred, intercept restored). Features = residue indicators mod {3,4,5,7,8,11,12,13,840} scaled 1/sqrt(m), ridge lambda CV-tuned, 80/20 split, seed 1968, R(p) from exact divisor count on 4p+1, primes 5..10^5 with p=1 mod 4 (4783 primes). Held-out R^2: all-moduli kernel 0.642, mod-840 class mean 0.569. Control with moduli {17,19,840} (seed 19681) gains a comparable amount over its own class-mean baseline (0.623 vs 0.584), so the extra gain is regularisation/additive shrinkage, not a modulus-specific signal from 11, 13.
not_done: Single split and single seed for main and control; the squared-coefficient weights are not scale-comparable across moduli (features scaled 1/sqrt(m)), so no per-modulus weight ranking is claimed.
next: Repeat over several seeds with per-modulus held-out gain to see whether 11 and 13 separate from the control.

summary: Round 3 with exact R(p) (ordered divisor pairs of 4p+1 with both factors = 3 mod 4), N<10^4 gives 2067 primes p=n^2+n+41 with p=1 mod 4 (max p ~ 10^8). Compared with 2067 residue-matched controls (same p mod 840 counts, drawn from all primes =1 mod 4 up to the same max): family mean R 7.38 vs control 8.73, median 4 vs 6, Mann-Whitney p = 7e-4. The Euler family has systematically lower R, and a plausible mechanism exists: 4p+1 = (2n+1)^2 + 164, so every prime divisor of 4p+1 must split in Q(sqrt(-41)) (since 164 = 4*41), which biases the divisor-residue statistic that R counts. Only one control draw was used.
not_done: Repeated control draws; check that the mechanism (split-in-Q(sqrt(-41)) restriction) accounts for the full gap, e.g. by comparing with primes p where (2n+1)^2+164 is replaced by a generic quadratic x^2+164-type value of the same size; no conclusion about ES itself.
next: Repeat controls over 20 seeds and compare against a second Euler-type family with a different discriminant (e.g. n^2+n+17 or n^2+n+11) to test whether the gap tracks the discriminant.

summary: Round 3: statistic R(p)/(log p)^2 over primes p=1 mod 4 up to 10^7 (R = ordered divisor pairs x,y=3 mod 4 with xy=4p+1). Nested classes 1 mod 840 (3426 primes), 1 mod 9240 (345), 1 mod 120120 (23). The 840-class mean (0.0133) is far below its complement (0.0235), but the complement is not residue-matched (4p+1 mod small primes is fixed inside the class), so this gap reflects local congruence structure, not self-similarity. The only matched controls are inside the 840 class: 9240-subclass 0.0104 vs 0.0139 (2.7 SE, p=0.007, uncorrected for three tests), 120120 subclass n=23 too small to read.
not_done: A residue-matched control for the 840-class itself (no exact match exists); R/M per-prime witness normalisation (the statistic is R/(log p)^2, not the item's R/M_BM); primes beyond 10^7 in the 120120 class.
next: Compare R/(log p)^2 across all 840-classes against their local-congruence signature (4p+1 mod 840) to separate self-similarity from congruence effects.

summary: Round 3: discriminant D=-16c^2d, 1<=c,d<=20 (400 pairs), class number by reduced-form count; witness = divisor f of p^2+4c^2d with 1<f<N and f = -p mod 4cd, primes p=1 mod 4 up to 10^4 (609). Witness cases have even h in all 9371 observations, which looked significant (chi^2 p=8e-7), but h depends only on (c,d), so the 243600 per-prime observations are not independent. At the level of pairs there is exactly one odd-h pair, (c,d)=(1,1), h=1, with witness rate 0; Fisher p=1.0. No class-group parity correlation is supported; the earlier 'significant' value is a one-pair artifact.
not_done: Larger (c,d) ranges where odd class numbers occur more often; the witness predicate is taken from the item's Type-I form (f | p^2+4c^2d, f = -p mod 4cd) as I read it.
next: Test the same statistic over a larger (c,d) box (d squarefree, c up to 200) so that odd-h pairs are numerous enough for a pair-level test.

summary: Round 3: Ozsvath-Szabo recursion for d(L(p,A),i) (closed form checked at q=1), statistic S(p,A)=sum_i d(L(p,A),i) over length-3 A, primes p=1 mod 4, 5<=p<2000. Raw sums scale like p^2 and the QR/QNR pooled comparison is confounded by p, so the test is within-prime: S/p^2, QR mean 0.00862 vs QNR 0.00561; QR larger for 87 of 133 primes (sign test p=4.8e-4). The sign-conditioned split is therefore a real within-prime effect in the d-invariant sums.
not_done: Identification of sum_i d(L(p,A),i) with a Dedekind-sum/Casson-Walker expression (not verified); the test is one-sided on the length-3 restriction only; no selector built.
next: Check numerically whether sum_i d(L(p,A),i) is an affine function of the Dedekind sum s(A,p) (or s(A^-1,p)); if so the signal is the already-covered Dedekind-sum structure of DEDEKIND_ES.md, if not it is new.
